paper.title: MBA-SLAM: Motion Blur Aware Gaussian Splatting SLAM

adoption.rationale: WU-CVGL/MBA-SLAM is the authors' official release of the complete MBA-SLAM pipeline, containing the motion-blur-aware tracker and the NeRF/3DGS mappers, and it has the largest community following among all genuine implementations surveyed (78 stars versus 0 for the only other full-code fork).

candidates.note: The authors' official implementation of the complete MBA-SLAM pipeline, including the motion-blur-aware tracker and both NeRF- and 3DGS-based mappers.
A full fork of the official repository with the identical complete source tree and README, preserving the exact MBA-SLAM implementation.
A stale fork that contains only the original project-page README and assets, with no source code or runnable implementation.
Another stale fork containing only the original project-page README and assets, not the implementation.

MBA-VO is the authors' earlier motion-blur-aware visual odometry work; it tracks exposure-time camera trajectories but has no dense NeRF/3DGS mapper, so it is a precursor rather than a full MBA-SLAM implementation.
BAD-Gaussians performs bundle-adjusted deblurring of a fixed blurry image set with 3D Gaussian splatting; it is an offline reconstruction component, not the dense visual SLAM pipeline of MBA-SLAM.
BAD-NeRF performs bundle-adjusted deblurring of a fixed image set with a neural radiance field; it lacks the tracker and SLAM system that define MBA-SLAM.
An accelerated nerfstudio reimplementation of BAD-NeRF; it is a deblurring component, not an implementation of MBA-SLAM's SLAM pipeline.
CoMoGaussian models continuous camera motion for 3D Gaussian splatting from motion-blurred images, but it is a reconstruction method without SLAM tracking or mapping.

Deblur-SLAM is a separate monocular deblurring Gaussian-splatting SLAM method; it shares blur vocabulary but is not an implementation of MBA-SLAM's RGB-D pipeline with its MBA-VO-style motion-blur-aware tracker.
Unblur-SLAM is a separate CVPR 2026 dense neural SLAM method that handles blurry inputs using DROID-SLAM plus an EVSSM deblurring network; its problem setting and blur modelling differ from MBA-SLAM.
TRGS-SLAM targets IMU-aided Gaussian-splatting SLAM for thermal, rolling-shutter and noisy images using B-spline trajectories, a different problem setting and model.
